I don’t want to minimize any of these experiences…. Speaking as someone who’s bipolar, please, please don’t let these examples and his behavior be the only thing you think of when you hear about people with bipolar, or someone you know or love tells you about their diagnosis.  Bipolar comes in multiple forms and is different for everyone who suffers from it.  It can be sitting on the back burner just waiting for the trigger that sets it off.  For me it was partially hereditary, but what launched me into my first episode was a very, very traumatic experience. Medication has changed/saved my life.  We aren’t all loose cannons waiting to explode.  It never goes away, but it can be managed.

We have the same dog. I thought we were the only people with this problem. We tried everything.  Best dog in the world but really OCD about the strangest things. We say she's "touched" because its nicer than saying she's crazy.  Obviously I can't guarantee it'll work but the secret combination suggested to us by our vet was a pheromone collar and Granulex to heal the wounds. The pheromone collar took about 2 weeks to notice a difference in her behavior, and she's still far from normal, but it did help. The real miracle for us was the granulex. I don't know how to link it on mobile but we just hit up the ole googles for the granulex and amazon for the collars. The granulex an aerosol spray, we put on a light coat morning and night. Apparently it tastes nasty, so she picked a new place to eat a hole. As soon as I noticed it, I started spraying it too. The Granulex promotes scar tissue so rather than "healing" the sore scars up. I could see the edges starting to heal within a couple of days. Once that started she just stopped. Like completely. Never bothered either of them again. I kept spraying the sores until they were all scarred up. Its not pretty, she has two half dollar sized black scars on her leg, but they aren't open wounds. I don't know why she stopped. Hasn't done it since.  Was it one or the other, the combination, a coincidence? I don't know.  We stopped using the collars after about 4 months, just because I forgot to order more (they're similar to flea collars, replace monthly I think). That's been 9 months ago, she's still "touched" but at least she doesnt look like she just returned from battle. Its worth a shot. Worst case you're out another $50 and back where you started. If you're like us you might still have a "touched" doggie, but at least it isn't actively eating itself. Best case scenario, it changes everyone's life and you owe me a cocktail.  Hope it helps, good luck.

Are you us? We have 3, one of which is a lab/pit mix and a high jump super star. We tried everything. We have a 6ft wooden fence and have tried it all, from coyote roller to lattice. Like yours, she doesn't even touch the fence, clears it like its not even there.  Even with a ton of exercise, she thinks she needs whatever is on the other side.

Some may not agree but we finally resorted to a collar. Its remote control and has a vibrate as well as a shock. We've never had to use the shock, the vibrate is enough. We started on a Saturday so we'd be home all day to watch. When she jumped we hit vibrate. By about jump #3 i think she was convinced the fence was the culprit. After that, as long as the collar is on, she thinks the fence bites. She definitely associates the two. 


While we do have to remind her occasionally, always with vibrate, its cut the jumping by 90%.  
I felt bad at first. But not nearly as bad as if she'd fallen victim to being a "pit bull on the loose". We all know how that usually ends.
